title: Who Am I?
content:
One quiet evening, Leo was sitting alone in a small park.

The sky was dark, but the stars were beautiful.

Leo looked at the sky and started thinking.

“Who **am I**?” he asked himself.

He was a student, a son, and a friend.

But was that everything?

“**Am I** happy?” he wondered.

Leo didn't know the answer.

His life **wasn't** perfect, and he **wasn't** always confident.

Sometimes, he felt lost.

“**Is** it normal to feel lost?” he asked.

An old man sitting nearby heard him.

“Yes,” the man said. “We **are not** always sure about who we are.”

Leo looked at him.

“**Are** you happy?” he asked.

The old man smiled.

“I **am**, but I **wasn't** always happy.”

“Why not?”

“Because I thought life **was** about having all the answers,” the man replied.

“And it isn't?”

“No. Life **isn't** a test with only one correct answer.”

Leo remained silent.

The old man looked at the stars.

“We **are** always changing,” he said. “You **are not** the same person you were yesterday.”

Leo thought about those words.

“So, **am I** supposed to know everything?”

The old man laughed.

“Of course not. You **aren't** supposed to have all the answers.”

For the first time that evening, Leo smiled.

Maybe life **wasn't** about finding one perfect answer.

Maybe the questions were just as important.

And perhaps the most important question was not:

**“Who am I?”**

But:

**“Who am I becoming?”**
